title: The push of a beam on a surface that absorbs it
spoken: The force on an absorbing surface equals the power divided by c.
explanation: A 1 W beam, absorbed, pushes with 1 divided by 299 792 458, about 3.34 times ten to the minus nine newtons.
assumptions: A steady beam arriving head on, at a surface at rest.
A foundation lesson's statement in modern notation; not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: Power over c
notes.explanation: Energy per second, turned into momentum per second by dividing by c.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Momentum arriving each second is a force.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: Light of energy E carries momentum E over c.

notes.title: Push on an absorbing surface
notes.explanation: The force of the beam on a surface that keeps its light.

notes.title: Power of the beam
notes.explanation: The light energy arriving each second.
